items.title: UAE bans all Iranian nationals from entry and transit

featured_image.name: UAE bars all Iranian passport holders from entry and transit ...

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates has imposed a sweeping ban on all Iranian passport holders from entering or transiting through the country, with major carriers Emirates, Etihad Airways, and FlyDubai confirming the restriction in updated travel notices, according to Iran International. The directive, which took immediate effect, bars Iranian nationals regardless of visa category — including holders of valid residency, tourist, and visit visas.[1]

The ban means Iranian nationals currently outside the UAE, including long-term residents, will be denied re-entry, with the restriction reflected in official immigration application responses. Emirates confirmed that Iranian nationals are "not permitted to enter or transit through the UAE," though it noted an exception for holders of Golden Visas, according to a statement reported by Al Arabiya.[2][1]

items.title: Syria vows to stay out of US-Israeli war on Iran unless attacked

featured_image.name: Syria will stay out of Iran conflict unless it faces ...

items.description:
Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa declared on Tuesday that Syria will not enter the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran unless the country comes under direct attack, positioning Damascus as a bystander in a regional conflict now in its second month.

"Unless Syria is targeted by any party, Syria will remain outside any conflict," al-Sharaa said during a speech at the Chatham House think tank in London, where he outlined his vision for the country's future. "We had enough war. We paid a large bill. We are not ready for another war experience".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran demands full end to war, rejects ceasefire talks

featured_image.name: Abbas Araghchi | Iran, Education, Life, Biography, War, & Nuclear Diplomacy  | Britannica

items.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi drew a firm line on Tuesday against any temporary pause in the month-long conflict with the United States and Israel, insisting Tehran will accept nothing less than a complete end to hostilities across the region. "We will not accept a ceasefire but rather seek a complete end to the war, not in Iran alone but in the entire region," Araghchi said, according to statements reported by Al Jazeera and confirmed by multiple outlets.[1][2][3]

In an interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi confirmed that messages have been exchanged with the U.S. — including with American envoy Steve Witkoff — but stressed that such contacts "do not mean that we are in negotiations". He added that Iran has "zero" trust in Washington's sincerity, citing the collapse of the 2015 nuclear deal.[1]

items.title: Explosions rock Damascus as Israel intercepts Iranian missiles over Syria

items.description: Explosions echoed across the Syrian capital Damascus on Tuesday as Israeli air defense systems intercepted Iranian missiles passing through Syrian airspace, according to a report by Syrian state television carried by Reuters. The blasts underscore how Syria, despite avoiding direct involvement in the wider US-Israel war on Iran, is increasingly caught in the crossfire of a conflict now in its 32nd day.[1][2]

items.title: King Charles to visit US amid Trump-UK rift over Iran war

featured_image.name: Donald Trump Gets Boost as King Charles Visit Confirmed

items.description:
Buckingham Palace confirmed on Tuesday that King Charles III and Queen Camilla will travel to the United States in late April for an official state visit, even as President Trump launched fresh attacks on Britain for refusing to join the military campaign against Iran.

The announcement came just minutes after Trump renewed his criticism of the UK and other European allies on Truth Social, telling them to "go get your own oil" from the Strait of Hormuz and warning that "the USA won't be there to help you anymore, just like you weren't there for us". Trump also urged Prime Minister Keir Starmer to "build up some delayed courage" and seize the strait, which has been largely closed since the Iran conflict began in late February.[1][2]

items.title: UN warns Lebanon at 'breaking point' as 1.1M displaced

featured_image.name: UN seeks $47 billion in aid as donor appetite shrinks while ...

items.description:
The United Nations' top humanitarian official warned the Security Council on Tuesday that Lebanon has reached a "breaking point," with more than 1.1 million people displaced and over 1,240 killed in the past four weeks as Israeli military operations intensify across the country.

Tom Fletcher, the UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs, briefed ambassadors from Beirut during an emergency session on March 31, describing "anxiety and tensions at levels I have not witnessed in many years" as airstrikes and drone activity continue to shake the Lebanese capital and surrounding areas.[1]

items.title: UK, Syria pledge to work with allies to reopen Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Keir Starmer meets Syrian president in Downing Street amid Middle ...

items.description: As the war between the United States and Israel on one side and Iran on the other enters its fifth week, UN Secretary-General António Guterres has intensified his calls for all parties to pull back from the brink, warning that the conflict has spiraled "out of control" and risks devastating consequences for civilians and the global economy alike. His appeals come as diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — closed by Iran since early March — gain new urgency, with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa pledging on Tuesday to "work with others to restore freedom of navigation" through the critical waterway.[1][2]
